findings.title: When "Hi, This Is IT" Comes Through Microsoft Teams
findings.summary_md: Palo Alto Networks Unit 42 documented how attackers abuse Microsoft Teams chat invitations to impersonate IT helpdesk staff. The report references a December 2025 Mandiant-tracked cluster (UNC6692) that convinced victims to accept external Teams chats. It explains the cross-tenant external unfamiliar tag and how screen-control features can be abused.

findings.title: Palo Alto Unit 42: Fake IT Support Abuses Teams to Deliver EtherRAT (June 28, 2026)
findings.summary_md: Unit 42 observed a campaign combining email phishing with a fake IT support Microsoft Teams call to deliver EtherRAT. The attacker used an external account (helpdesk@Progressive936.onmicrosoft.com), obtained remote screen control, guided the victim to install HopToDesk and AnyDesk, and delivered a malicious MSI (v7.msi) from camorreado.click that drops a blockchain-anchored C2 bot.

findings.title: UNC6692 Impersonates IT Help Desk via Microsoft Teams to Deploy SNOW Malware
findings.summary_md: Google Threat Intelligence Group and Mandiant reported threat cluster UNC6692 actively impersonating IT helpdesk staff over Microsoft Teams between March 1 and April 1, 2026. The campaign targeted 77% senior employees and led to malware deployment, data theft, and ransomware. The actors relied on Teams chat invitations from external accounts and social engineering rather than technical exploits.
